role: Main-file of the HRV detail screen pushed from the Dashboard HRV chip: hero RMSSD with z-score verdict, HR strip, autonomic capacity card, 30-day trend rows, plus the async loaders for the full RR series and the Beat Consistency priors baseline. Charts/engine-room/Beat Consistency card live in HRVDetailV2View+Charts.swift.
types: HRVDetailV2View.HRVVerdict: enum — Excellent/Good/Fair/Low verdict for today's RMSSD
toplevel: Stored-property initializers only: @ScaledMetric sizes bound to text styles (11..56pt), @State defaults (engineRoomTab=.timeDomain, flags false, arrays empty, optionals nil). EngineTab raw values are English strings 'Time','Frequency','Nonlinear','ANS','Quality'. Header doc (lines 4-22) claims a <256-beat Frequency-tab explanation and a >10% artifact caution banner; the banner is implemented at line 220, the frequency-tab copy lives in HRVDetailV2View+Charts.swift.

flags.text: Trend rows are labelled 'vs 30-day avg' (line 732) and the doc says 'mean of the last 30 days of overnight readings' (644), but the input `recentSessions` is the dashboard's 35-most-recent sessions of ANY type (MainTabView.swift:710, DashboardV2View.swift:430). For a user with workouts/quick readings, the average covers far fewer than 30 days of overnight nights — the same truncation the file itself fixed for Beat Consistency priors (lines 332-335) but not here.

units.does: Retrieves the full session off-main via RRCollector; if it has a non-empty rrSeries stores it in fullRRSeries; then builds sampled plot points from effectiveRRSeries and sets rrLoadCompleted.

branches.cond: full session found AND rrSeries non-nil AND points non-empty
branches.effect: true: fullRRSeries = series; false: fullRRSeries is NOT touched and is NOT reset by loadDetail (HRVDetailV2View.swift:265-269 resets only the flags/priors/result), so on an in-place session change it still holds the PREVIOUS session's series and effectiveRRSeries (line 103) returns it; retrieve failure is swallowed (retrieveOrLog logs and returns nil)

flags.text: fullRRSeries is never reset when session.id changes (loadDetail resets every other piece of state at 266-269 but not fullRRSeries), and loadRRSeries has no cancellation check after its await. When the dashboard's hrvDestination swaps in a newer latestOvernightComplete under the same view identity, (a) a failed/empty full retrieve for the new session leaves the old night's RR series in place, and (b) the cancelled old task's retrieve can finish after the new one and overwrite fullRRSeries with the old night. The waveform, Poincaré plot and the Beat Consistency score (scoreNight reads effectiveRRSeries at 381) then show the previous night's beats under the new night's header.

units.does: Collects up to 28 prior overnight session ids, asks the shared BeatConsistencyPriorsCache to warm them, polls for cached features, then (if not cancelled) stores priors, scores tonight off-main, and sets baselineLoadCompleted.

branches.effect: true: returns without storing (view gone); false: stores results

flags.text: startWarm returns immediately when a walk is already running (BeatConsistencyPriorsCache.swift:255), so ids for THIS session are not queued if another walk is in flight; waitForPriors then waits on the unrelated walk and the card resolves to 'Calibrating' until a later open re-warms.

priorBaselineFeatures is write-only: it is assigned at 268 and 327 and never read anywhere in the repo (the card reads beatConsistencyComputed); the @State and its doc comment (79-87) describe a role it no longer has.

Polls the priors cache every 0.5 s (max 40 ticks ≈20 s) until min(minNightsForLowConfidence, ids.count) priors are cached or the warm walk ends; returns all cached features for the ids and logs a debug summary.

branches.cond: cachedCount < needed AND cache.isWarming AND waitedTicks < 40
branches.effect: true: sleep 0.5 s and recount; false: stop waiting (enough cached, walk finished, or 20 s elapsed) and return what is cached
true: breaks out of loop, returns partial result; false: continue

flags.text: trendAverageOptional is a copy of trendAverage differing only in the KeyPath value type (Double? vs Double), including the duplicated comment block.

Average does not filter isReliableForHRVAggregates, while the Compare-to-history sheet for the same metrics does (MetricInfoSheets.swift:476); unreliable overnight nights (high artifact) widen the trend baseline here but not there.

The same screen gives two different 'vs your usual' figures for RMSSD: the hero subtitle compares against the tracker's geometric baseline exp(lnRmssdMean) over up to 60 nights (445-447), while the RMSSD trend row compares against the arithmetic mean of overnight sessions in the dashboard's 35-session slice (652-669, label 732). The Morning Results trend card was changed specifically to use the tracker baseline so these resolve to one number (TrendComparisonCard.swift:186-201); this screen was not.
